Figma's API returns 400 for .make files, so the poster reverse-engineered the undocumented binary. It is a ZIP with a custom format: Deflate for the schema chunk, Zstandard for the data, then Kiwi binary decoding. They published scripts to extract the React apps.

The extractor post lists cases where you'd need to get code out of Figma Make yourself: a client hands you a Figma Make prototype but not the design file, you want to audit AI-generated code before deployment, or you need to migrate away from Figma Make to a different stack.

A commenter noted that Figma Make's AI writes React code rather than creating a Figma drawing. They suggested that all the training on code has made it easier for the AI to write the app than to make an illustration of it.

A commenter said Figma Make was "definitely late to market compared to V0 and loveable." They added that Figma's focus on the existing designer market makes sense short-term, but other startups may solve end-user programming before Figma does.
